successful: Reverified the official St Andrews item record and exact manuscript label transcription 'Panis 383'.
Reverified the BHL item and article bibliographic range 238-253.
Confirmed from the existing complete catalogue parse that 383 lies inside the derived Mammalia block 373-405.
blocked: Search-index access did not surface the individual BHL page OCR/image containing row 383.
The available web interface exposed the book/article container but not the decisive row text in a retrievable form during this pass.
verification_attempt.result: The numerical/taxonomic alignment remains structurally plausible but is not an item-level catalogue-number closure.

critical_guard.do_not_expand_panis: Do not normalize or expand the St Andrews transcription 'Panis' to pancreas, penis, an abbreviation or another anatomical term without the slide image and historical row wording.
critical_guard.do_not_treat_383_as_catalogue_number_yet: The number is only a candidate Naples catalogue address until row 383 is read directly and label grammar is compared with other Station slides.
critical_guard.taxonomy_note: The historical label Delphinus phocaena is sufficient for object-side comparison; modern taxonomic normalization is a separate layer and should not replace the historical wording in the crosswalk.

cheap_next_test: Retrieve the page image/OCR for catalogue row 383 from BHL item 37442 or Internet Archive mittheilungenaus02staz.
Record rows 382-384 verbatim, including price column, preparation/anatomical wording and any ditto marks.
Compare row 383 against both St Andrews Delphinus phocaena BPM/1/T8/6 and the separate St Andrews Delphinus slide BPM/1/U12/12/B/1/7 whose label explicitly includes SKIN.
Check whether other St Andrews Naples slides carry a comparable right-label number grammar before interpreting 383 as a catalogue number.
research_payoff: The failed cheap test is still useful because it prevents a false S-level closure. The slide already preserves three distinct address layers—Naples institutional/taxonomic labelling, the unresolved '383' inscription, and successive St Andrews storage addresses. Row 383 remains the single decisive missing relation.
